why: A server started through a shell with an inline command string runs anything the string says, and the string is where an attacker edits. The fail side launches a POSIX shell with an inline command and no acceptance, so it fails with the shell label. The pass side is the same launch with its exact fingerprint in .rebar-injection-allowlist: a shell launch is reviewed and accepted, it is not one of the findings no entry can exempt. Whoever skips commands that are not package runners turns the fail side green; whoever makes the shell label unexemptable turns the pass side red.
